statusDefinitions.enforced: Every named control for the narrowly described current surface has implementation and automated verification evidence.
statusDefinitions.partial: Useful controls exist, but one or more documented attack paths or lifecycle requirements remain unqualified.
statusDefinitions.planned: The surface is not supported and must remain disabled until its acceptance criteria are implemented and verified.
statusDefinitions.release-blocked: The current controls are insufficient for production qualification of the named surface; the recorded gate must remain pending.

risks.title: Malformed or oversized project documents
risks.actor: A user or collaborator supplies a corrupt or adversarial project document.

currentControls.summary: Core project migration validates supported schemas and opens newer schemas read-only without overwriting them.
AUP4 conversion sanitizes imported records and is exercised with corrupt and compatibility fixtures.

A format-specific legacy `.aup` XML structural budget caps authoritative declared `File.size` and independently measures the returned text's UTF-8 byte length at 16 MiB, with at most 100,000 retained elements, 400,000 attributes, and maximum depth at 128 through lower-only test seams. Limits reject before any legacy `_data` block read, conversion, project/source persistence, or imported-project publication. This narrow control does not qualify elapsed time, other project families, selected `_data` bytes or decoded PCM amplification, or the total import working set.

Supported canonical, default-sized legacy `.aup` simple and silent block materialization has non-raiseable production ceilings and lower-only test seams: 65,536 selected companion files and 65,536 materializing references, 2 MiB per referenced physical file, 1 MiB per AU sample payload, 524,288 decoded or silent frames per block, 512 MiB of authoritative unique referenced `File.size`, and 512 MiB of retained Float32 PCM including repeated references, silence, and linked-track zero-fill. Bounded exact/basename indexes prevent reference-by-file lookup multiplication; positive block lengths, the 24-byte AU header minimum, and equal-length paired linked clips are required. Checked admission covers selected/reference counts, declared bytes, and retained PCM before retained-PCM allocation or block reads, while AU payload/frame checks precede decoded-block allocation. Actual `ArrayBuffer.byteLength` must equal snapshotted declared size. Audacity's native-endian AU representation is accepted, each unique file is read and decoded once, and one preallocated output per physical clip makes the logically reachable parser-owned pending window beyond retained PCM at most one 2 MiB encoded file plus one 2 MiB decoded block. Equal or admitted zero-padded linked channels pass conversion without channel-normalization copies. Refusal precedes conversion, project/source persistence, and imported-project publication. This format-specific control does not qualify XML-tree or opaque-extension clone amplification, elapsed time or cancellation, aliases, customized Audacity block-size settings above the policy ceilings, provider-internal copies or garbage-collection lag, downstream conversion/waveform/storage/persistence working sets, total renderer RSS, noncanonical AU padding, other project families, or streaming-scale legacy import.

residualRisks.exposure: Legacy `.aup` XML and supported canonical, default-sized simple/silent `_data` materialization now have format-specific structural, referenced-input, block-geometry, retained-PCM, indexed-lookup, and parser-owned pending-window budgets. Other supported project parsers still do not share aggregate byte, node, depth, or elapsed-time budgets, while XML-tree and opaque-extension cloning, aliases, customized Audacity block sizes above policy ceilings, provider-internal allocation, downstream conversion/waveform/storage/persistence amplification, garbage-collection lag, total renderer RSS, cancellation, and streaming-scale legacy import remain outside this qualification.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Apply documented per-format and aggregate byte, node, depth, elapsed-time, cancellation, and end-to-end working-set budgets before persistence, including remaining project families and downstream legacy-import work.
acceptanceCriteria: Remaining project-family boundary tests reject oversized and deeply nested fixtures before writes, and qualified aggregate, cancellation, elapsed-time, and end-to-end working-set budgets cover parser orchestration and downstream materialization.

residualRisks.exposure: Focused legacy `.aup` XML and AU-block boundary/no-publication fixtures cover declared and returned XML bytes, elements, attributes, depth, selected and referenced counts, indexed lookup and ambiguity, declared/actual block bytes and the header minimum, positive block and payload/frame geometry, native endianness, pre-allocation refusal, retained PCM, silence, repeated references, stereo padding, and unequal linked-pair rejection, but the maintained malformed-project corpus does not yet cover every supported project family.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Maintain regression and fuzz fixtures for each supported project parser.
acceptanceCriteria: CI runs parser corpus tests with storage publication assertions for each family.

risks.title: Malformed media and metadata consume excessive resources or escape validation
risks.actor: An imported audio, video, metadata, or codec-argument payload is corrupt or adversarial.

currentControls.summary: WAV chunk iteration, metadata sizes, channel counts, and compressed ADM XML expansion have explicit bounds.
Custom FFmpeg exports use allowlisted protocols and reject extra inputs, reports, and unbounded arguments.

residualRisks.exposure: Compressed audio and video decoders lack a broad maintained malformed-input corpus and resource-budget gate.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Add codec-family corpus tests and explicit decode memory, output, and elapsed-time budgets.
acceptanceCriteria: CI exercises truncated, oversized, recursive, and decompression-amplification fixtures without publishing partial output.

residualRisks.exposure: Future native decoding is not yet isolated from the UI process or covered by crash quarantine.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Run native decoders in a supervised helper with bounded IPC and documented OS sandbox policy.
acceptanceCriteria: Helper crash, timeout, oversized output, and malformed-message tests leave the editor process responsive.

risks.title: Portable project archive paths and descriptors reference unintended or altered content
risks.actor: A .scape archive contains unsafe names, duplicates, inconsistent descriptors, or altered payload bytes.

currentControls.summary: Import rejects absolute, backslash, traversal, and duplicate names, validates manifest descriptors, and verifies extracted size and SHA-256 before publishing the project.

Import and inspection share a strict metadata envelope that rejects encrypted and directory entries, duplicate source or entry ownership, reserved-entry reuse, descriptor aliases, missing entries, and unreferenced extra entries before project or source storage writes.

After project migration, import and inspection require equal source/descriptor counts, unique exact case-sensitive source IDs, and identical audio/video kinds before collision handling, transaction creation, or any storage call.

risks.title: Portable project archive expansion exhausts memory, storage, or execution time
risks.actor: A .scape archive uses large metadata, misleading sizes, compression amplification, or a malicious PCM header.

currentControls.summary: Import caps entry count, validates hashes after extraction, aborts a failing audio writer, deletes already staged sources, and saves the project last.
A strict TypeScript envelope validates the entry-count limit and safe integer compressed/uncompressed metadata for every file before reading manifest bytes.
Manifest JSON is capped at 32 MiB and project JSON at 256 MiB using both central-directory preflight and byte-counted streaming text sinks.
The envelope rejects central-directory declarations whose safe cumulative uncompressed size exceeds 64 GiB before reading any entry body.

One shared budget counts bytes actually emitted into the manifest, project, and every extracted asset sink, rejecting cumulative output above 64 GiB before the over-budget chunk is retained or published.

Audio extraction validates each four-byte frame header against the shared 65,536-frame and 64-channel geometry limits before checked byte-length calculation or allocation; parser-owned pending storage is capped at 16 MiB plus the header.

Before manifest extraction, every entry runs zip.js strict local-header validation and pairwise entry-range overlap detection without decompressing its body; tested method disagreements and nested entry ranges reject before storage work.

A bounded raw-layout preflight, under a shared non-raiseable 33 MiB central-directory cap, anchors exact classic/Zip64 end and central-directory records, validates every central/local header and data descriptor without reading payloads, and rejects gaps, overlap, or entry ranges crossing the central directory before zip.js construction. Export admission reserves the pinned writer's greater-than-4-GiB Zip64 offset branch so produced archives remain admissible.

Archive enumeration is hard-capped at 4,096 entries, bounding zip.js pairwise layout comparisons, and one archive-wide budget is capped at 65,536 canonical PCM chunks before another source-writer call or chunk allocation.
Every project or asset descriptor must exactly match its entry's declared uncompressed size before project JSON or asset extraction begins.
The manifest, project, and asset descriptors must own distinct expected entries, and all extra, alias, missing, directory, or reserved-name entries are rejected before storage work.
Any encrypted central-directory entry rejects the archive before manifest or project bytes are read.
Inspection and import call the same strict archive-envelope validator; an integration test proves both reject the same extra entry before storage writes.
Central-directory indexing requires ZIP STORE and equal compressed/uncompressed sizes before local-header preflight or body reads; canonical exports pin the same policy.

Original video entries emit at most 4 MiB per zip.js chunk, are charged and independently hashed before each awaited transactional storage write, and must match declared size and SHA-256 before publication. OPFS receives bounded writes; IndexedDB uses source-owned native Blob chunks; process-memory fallback rejects payloads above 64 MiB before extraction. Cancellation, metadata drift, and failed publication remove staging and preserve prior inventory.

Canonical save output is re-chunked to at most 4 MiB, constrained by the admitted archive maximum, and verified by independent byte counts before publication. File System Access and desktop project targets remain staged until an explicit commit; desktop additionally negotiates one-MiB acknowledged IPC writes and synced rename. The non-streaming browser-download fallback retains its non-raiseable 512 MiB final-Blob ceiling.

The tested .scape open/save path propagates one task AbortSignal through ZIP enumeration and extraction, source reads and writes, archive output, and file publication. Cancellation closes readers, returns source iterators, aborts unpublished destinations and audio writers, deletes provisional media, and restores the prior project plus its retained revisions.

risks.title: Current Electron renderer IPC reaches privileges outside the versioned bridge
risks.actor: Compromised renderer content attempts to invoke arbitrary Electron or Node.js capabilities.

currentControls.summary: The renderer has context isolation, no Node integration, a sandbox, and a frozen input-validating v1 bridge.
Main-process handlers require the expected webContents and root document URL while navigation, new windows, webviews, and unapproved permissions are denied.

risks.title: Current desktop static-resource requests escape the packaged application root
risks.actor: Renderer content crafts an encoded path, symlink path, method, or range request.

currentControls.summary: Static requests are decoded, canonicalized, constrained by realpath containment, limited to safe methods, and protected by the desktop CSP.

risks.title: Desktop read capabilities leak paths, outlive their owner, or allow unbounded working sets
risks.actor: Compromised renderer content reuses or accumulates capabilities, or triggers a large whole-file read.

currentControls.summary: User selection opens a regular file first, returns a high-entropy expiring token rather than a path, and serves bounded single ranges from the pinned handle.

Every pending or published desktop read capability is bound to the opaque main-owned identity of the currently committed main-frame document. For each committed-document owner, the store reserves one of at most 128 pending or live capability slots before its first file-open await. Before descriptor publication it checks that the owner's aggregate declared selected-file bytes remain at or below the non-raiseable 512 MiB ceiling and that the owner remains active. Wrong-owner release refuses without revealing, removing, or closing the capability. Correct release and expiry synchronously remove the capability from lookup before draining its handle. Main-frame non-same-document navigation, renderer loss, actual window close, and application shutdown synchronously fence the affected owner or store and remove its published capabilities from lookup before draining every admitted open and handle close. A delayed dialog or open or stat completion after owner revocation closes its candidate without publication. Partial multi-file registration drains every rollback release and reports the primary and cleanup failures. OS-open paths remain serially deduplicated at a visible queue head until delivery to a current ready owner. Count or byte exhaustion deterministically refuses the new admission without evicting an existing handle. Revocation and shutdown attempt every close before rejecting on cleanup failure; shutdown permanently refuses new admission.

Authoritative main-process admission limits aggregate active declared selected-file bytes to a non-raiseable 512 MiB per committed-document owner before descriptor publication. The preload sanitizes descriptor size as a safe non-negative integer within that ceiling, and the renderer materializer repeats admission before fetch, requires exact declared Content-Length, emitted-byte, and final Blob-size agreement, and reads only the response body stream. Retained response parts are copied and split at the non-raiseable 16 MiB platform media-chunk limit. The materializer forwards the caller-provided AbortSignal, promptly races and cancels a stalled body read with its exact reason, and never calls response.blob(). A scoped descriptor batch releases every capability after its callback on success, failure, or cancellation, while request abort destroys the corresponding protocol file stream. This is a bounded whole-Blob tier for the current surface, not a bound on decoder amplification or whole-process RSS; larger range-backed reads remain outside the qualified surface.

risks.title: Desktop saves overwrite unintended paths, leave partial files, or exhaust disk
risks.actor: Compromised renderer content reuses a target or sends inconsistent, oversized, or interrupted chunks.

currentControls.summary: A user-selected target becomes a short-lived single-use token; sequential one-MiB chunks are checked against an exact length and committed by synced same-directory rename with abort cleanup.

Only project save capabilities may select bounded streaming mode. Main rejects writes above the archive-admitted maximum, waits for an active chunk acknowledgement before abort cleanup, and removes sessions on navigation, renderer loss, window close, or shutdown; explicit finish remains the sync-and-rename commit boundary.

Shutdown synchronously rejects new target and save-session admission, drains operations admitted before the fence through any sync-and-rename commit, aborts remaining or late-opened staging, and exposes one idempotent disposal barrier that rejects on unacknowledged handle close or staging removal.

Every target and derived session is bound to one committed main-document owner. Owner revocation on main-document navigation, renderer loss, or actual window close synchronously fences admission, invalidates unconsumed targets including delayed dialog results, drains admitted begin, chunk, finish, and abort operations through any admitted sync-and-rename commit, then aborts remaining staging. Fresh-owner session admission waits for that drain so a stale commit cannot overtake a replacement save.

Main enforces 16 outstanding product-wide targets, 4 pending or live sessions, and 65 GiB per-save and aggregate admitted bytes, covering the canonical 64 GiB expanded `.scape` envelope plus its bounded STORE/ZIP overhead. Global count and byte reservations are taken synchronously before the first await, and production ceilings expose lower-only test seams. A fail-closed bigint `statfs` available-space check completes before staging open. The check is point-in-time admission, not an operating-system reservation; charges release only after no staging was acquired, an acknowledged cleanup, or a completed commit, and a staging cleanup failure leaves them charged.

residualRisks.exposure: A bounded IPC chunk must finish or fail before abort closes staging; sync/rename is the non-cancellable commit boundary, and parent-directory durability is not qualified.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Define the cancellation acknowledgement and platform durability contract for active save operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Fault-injection tests cover cancellation during write, sync, and rename on every supported desktop platform.

risks.title: Current user-authored Nyquist source escapes its bounded WebAssembly worker envelope
risks.actor: A Nyquist program loops, requests excessive memory or output, or attempts file access.

currentControls.summary: Nyquist runs in a dedicated worker with validated protocol and source/input/output bounds, a 256-MiB WebAssembly memory ceiling, timeout and abort termination, and disabled C file-I/O stubs.

risks.title: Future third-party Web effect packages gain same-origin JavaScript authority
risks.actor: A future reviewed effect package is malicious, compromised, or has a confused-deputy import surface.

currentControls.summary: The maintained registry currently exposes only reviewed, source-pinned bundled Nyquist plug-ins; no generic package loader exists.

residualRisks.exposure: A reviewed Web effect package ABI, import allowlist, signature/hash policy, revocation model, and worker lifecycle are not implemented.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Instantiate pure WebAssembly packages in dedicated workers through a minimal allowlisted host ABI; do not import arbitrary third-party JavaScript into the application origin.
acceptanceCriteria: Malformed ABI, forbidden import, timeout, oversized output, hash mismatch, and revocation tests pass before a package loader is exposed.

risks.title: Future native media and render helpers compromise the UI process or remain alive after cancellation
risks.actor: Malformed input, a compromised helper binary, or a protocol peer sends invalid messages or refuses shutdown.

currentControls.summary: The current versioned preload bridge exposes no native helper, process-spawn, or plug-in-host channel.

residualRisks.exposure: No bounded helper protocol, process supervisor, sandbox policy, crash quarantine, or binary attestation exists.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Define a versioned bounded IPC protocol and supervised process lifecycle with least-privilege OS policy and verified binaries.
acceptanceCriteria: Crash, hang, malformed message, oversized payload, binary mismatch, and cancellation tests pass without exposing raw spawn authority to the renderer.

risks.title: Future native audio or video plug-ins execute with ambient user-account authority
risks.actor: A third-party VST3, CLAP, AU, LV2, or OFX binary is malicious, vulnerable, or incompatible.

currentControls.summary: The current renderer bridge and editor registry expose no native plug-in discovery, loading, or execution surface.

residualRisks.exposure: No plug-in discovery allowlist, quarantine, permissions, compatibility process, consent UX, or signing policy exists.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Treat native plug-ins as arbitrary code, isolate them in a supervised host, minimize filesystem and network authority, and disclose residual OS authority to the user.
acceptanceCriteria: Host compromise, crash recovery, denial, scanning, consent, revocation, and per-platform packaging tests pass before discovery is enabled.

risks.title: Cancelled or superseded jobs continue consuming resources or publish late results
risks.actor: A user cancels, switches projects, closes a renderer, or starts a replacement task while I/O is active.

currentControls.summary: Controller tasks receive AbortSignals and generation checks prevent stale results from replacing current UI state.

Native .scape open/save tasks pass their AbortSignal through archive, tested storage, and file publication boundaries; cancellation rolls staged assets and project revisions back before the task settles.

Public .scape inspection starts one distinct named controller task before archive work, snapshots caller options, and composes the caller signal with the owned signal. Replacement, project switching, and terminal disposal synchronously abort ownership; a post-await current-task check rejects signal-ignoring late results, and finally releases completed tasks. Inspection passes that signal into its project-collision read. The default store promptly races stalled database admission, aborts and drains an active read-only IndexedDB transaction, and preserves the exact cancellation reason. The service gives the defensive read-only Scape boundary a narrow retention capability; that boundary normalizes and registers an injected lookup with the same inspection admission in its synchronous read callback before returning the provider promise to the abort race, promptly rejects a signal-ignoring provider, closes its archive reader, and suppresses the late result or failure. Focused regressions also pin switch cancellation before awaited project work and verify composition-root routing.

Every public .scape inspection registers before its first await with a controller-level coordinator that retains current and superseded generations through archive-reader cleanup and registered injected collision-provider settlement. Project-switch admission synchronously installs a reference-counted temporary fence, cancels captured Scape tasks with one shared legacy supersession AbortError per admission, rejects later inspection admission, and drains every captured generation and retained provider continuation before project work; overlapping queued switches keep admission fenced until the last switch settles. Controller disposal installs a permanent fence with the exact lifetime reason and drains retained generations before engine and storage teardown. Only rejection with the exact registration abort reason is benign; provider fulfillment or rejection releases retention without replacing that primary outcome, cleanup failures reject the barrier after all captured generations settle, and disposal continues remaining teardown before rejecting.

Public .scape file opens start one replaceable request task before inspection and carry its signal through collision choice. The UI owns one opaque prompt and settles its exact identity only once. Replacement, project switching, and terminal disposal synchronously clear and reject pending prompts with exact cancellation reasons, while explicit user cancel resolves normally. Request ownership finishes before native open starts; expected lifecycle unwind is suppressed from generic errors, and the shared dialog shell provides safe initial focus, focus containment, Escape dismissal, and focus restoration.

Within one project-store instance, every streamed-writer begin that passes synchronous argument and signal validation registers with the per-store lifecycle before its first awaited backend operation. After staging preparation returns, the admission attaches its chunk-token or OPFS-path identity and terminal writer abort before begin can return. Clear establishes a temporary admission fence and close a permanent one; both reject later begins, signal and drain captured pre-staging begins, abort staged chunk or OPFS sinks and active writers, and cannot settle while a pre-fence begin could still return a live writer or publish late state. A cleanup failure rejects the maintenance barrier instead of reporting successful quiescence.

Within one AudioEditorProjectStore, the facade tracks one active clear and one shared close barrier. Clear establishes media maintenance and captures its backend-admission promise before its first wait. Close installs the permanent media fence and terminal facade state before its first await, then joins an already admitted clear. Concurrent close callers return the same terminal-cleanup promise, and an admitted clear retains its normal memory fallback when database availability fails while an unrelated pending database admission remains fenced when no clear is active. The overlap regressions prove clear settles before close and neither close caller settles before the captured media operation drains.

IndexedDB schema v5 publishes generation-fenced ownership before streamed chunk or OPFS staging exists. Chunk writes and immutable metadata publication validate the live lease in their mutation transaction; clear rotates the generation atomically, cleanup retains live identities and reclaims expired staging, and degraded memory mode never creates uncoordinated shared OPFS staging.

Every retained-media load registers synchronously with the same per-store lifecycle coordinator used by streamed writers before its first await. Clear holds a temporary admission fence and close a permanent fence; both signal captured loads through cancellation linked with the caller and await terminal settlement before data deletion or database close. The multi-chunk regression proves a digest that observes the maintenance abort cannot publish version-one provenance or return a payload after maintenance settles; a standalone clear then reopens admission while close remains terminal.

IndexedDB schema v6 atomically removes spoofable provenance fields from pre-cutover media rows; markerless rows expose no inherited hash, acquire one retryable version-zero Web-Crypto content claim, hash stored bytes in bounded four-MiB reads, and publish version-one SHA-256 only through a token-checked compare-and-set that rejects stale delete or replacement races.

Project saves choose one target before asynchronous flush, stream through a plan-aware bounded destination, abort staging on project switch or failure, compare independent exact byte counts, and perform one explicit non-cancellable publication commit. Cancellation after a successful commit is reported as committed without stale success UI.

residualRisks.exposure: The tested native .scape open/save and direct-save publication paths propagate and roll back cancellation, and public inspection and its post-inspection collision continuation now own cancellation and reject stale results. The default inspection collision lookup accepts the owned signal, promptly races stalled database admission, and aborts and drains its read-only IndexedDB transaction. The defensive Scape boundary also rejects signal-ignoring injected lookups promptly, closes the archive reader, and registers and retains the normalized provider promise in its synchronous read callback before returning it to the abort race; project switching and controller disposal join that provider settlement. A provider that ignores its signal may consume resources until settlement, and a never-settling provider can hold lifecycle barriers indefinitely because there is no provider deadline or admission cap. The bounded desktop materializer forwards a supplied signal and releases its capability on abort, but open and import orchestration does not consistently own or provide that signal; AUP4, broad storage operations, and remaining desktop transports also do not share the qualified end-to-end contract.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Propagate one signal through every long-job layer and acknowledge cancellation only after readers, writers, workers, and staged records are closed or rolled back.
acceptanceCriteria: Cancellation during read, parse, source write, project save, file write, and project switch leaves no late publication or orphaned session.

residualRisks.exposure: The collision dialog exposes a choice-level Cancel only after inspection. Active project I/O progress still has no consistently exposed user cancel action and close/navigation teardown contract.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Expose cancel for long project operations and bind teardown to navigation, renderer destruction, and application shutdown.
acceptanceCriteria: Browser and desktop workflow tests cancel an active import/export and verify prompt, recoverable return to the editor.

risks.title: Runtime binaries or release assets differ from reviewed source and policy
risks.actor: A compromised registry, build input, update source, or release process substitutes an executable artifact.

currentControls.summary: StaffPad, Nyquist, Parametric EQ, and WavPack record source and binary hashes and have fail-fast audit scripts.
Desktop packaging verifies copied FFmpeg runtime, manifest, and notice bytes before applying Electron fuses, and checks packaged ASAR integrity before preview smoke tests.

One checked-in, self-consistent FFmpeg runtime policy manifest binds the package and lock identity, exact JavaScript and WebAssembly byte lengths and SHA-256 digests, R2 bucket and base prefix, content types, immutable cache metadata, CORS policy, corresponding-source descriptor, aggregate notice, licensing and security matrices, licensing policy, threat model, release-severity policy, and LF checkout rules. The publisher separately derives a full-manifest-SHA release prefix and no-store final pointer under a fixed tested code policy. One shared validator rejects unknown, missing, unsafe, symbolic, stale, or tampered inputs before desktop preparation deletes its build root, before the current Soundscaper public desktop-release assembler reads its asset directory, or before the publisher invokes Wrangler. The assembler requires exact Soundscaper product/target manifests and a version-matched package inventory before network access. Desktop runtime staging is transactional, and both staging and upload consume private snapshots of bytes retained by validation. Electron Builder's beforePack hook rejects staged runtime-summary, manifest, or notice drift present when the hook runs; its afterPack hook independently revalidates the copied runtime inventory, manifest, and notice before fuse or signing work. Publication authorizations mirror the fail-closed licensing gates. Offline regressions prove invalid preflight never enters desktop assembly or invokes Wrangler, tested staged drift is rejected at beforePack, and post-copy tampering cannot reach fuse work. The manifest review marker and payload digest detect inconsistent edits but do not authenticate independent human approval.

residualRisks.exposure: The publisher's content-addressed layout and pointer contract are code-defined rather than bound as manifest fields, and remote writes have no conditional-create or read-back proof. The browser and release workflows still hard-code the 0.12.10 path instead of checking the manifest prefix or resolving and authenticating the pointer, and they retain no verified rollback version; asset-host mutation or a partial update can therefore deny or substitute the runtime.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Bind the release-path and pointer schema/cache contract in reviewed policy, resolve the final pointer at the consumer boundary, authenticate the full manifest and asset digests, make publication conditional and verify remote reads before pointer promotion, compare workflow and consumer configuration with the policy manifest, and retain the last complete verified version for rollback.
acceptanceCriteria: Cross-browser offline/runtime-cache tests reject altered or incomplete remote releases and recover through the last complete digest-verified version.

residualRisks.exposure: The review status, reviewer, date, and payload digest are self-declared in the same editable manifest. They prove internal consistency and detect stale linked evidence, but do not independently authenticate approval.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Require independent approval through protected repository and publication workflows, and bind a signature or immutable CI attestation to the full manifest digest before public authorization can become approved.
acceptanceCriteria: A publication attempt with no independently verifiable approval attestation fails before any remote operation, and an attestation for a different manifest digest is rejected.

residualRisks.exposure: Desktop preview artifacts are unsigned and update signing, notarization, rollback, and key-rotation procedures are not production-qualified.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Qualify signed update publication, platform signing/notarization, rollback, and key compromise response.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-platform release drills verify signature rejection, rollback, provenance, and key rotation before stable auto-update is enabled.
